subject: Inference pipeline qualification, auth & routing (Quantify Labs POC)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sunil Park <s.park@quantifylabs.com>; Eva Martinez <eva@quantifylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + POC checklist (auth, routing, tool-calling)

Hi Sunil / Eva — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Recap and proposed next steps so we have a single reference for the POC kickoff. I focused this around the integration topics you flagged (SDK & auth, routing, structured tool output, embeddings + reranker).

Key takeaways from today
- Primary use case: customer support triage + knowledge retrieval. Live chat front-end that calls an LLM to classify intent, call external tools (ticket_lookup, product_search), and present a ranked list of candidate KB passages.
- Constraints: must run in Quantify VPC (private peering), SSO via your Azure AD/Okta, and <50ms median token latency target for 99th percentile chat paths.

POC success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: end-to-end demo where chat triggers 1) tool calls (ticket_lookup, price_check) and 2) reranker uses embeddings to surface top 3 KB passages.
- Performance: 95th percentile response <400ms for simple classify + tool proxy, cost estimate <= $X/token for peak workloads (we'll refine).
- Security: proof of auth via OIDC client-credentials and audit logs exported to your Splunk/ELK.

Integration checklist / asks for your infra team
1) SDK & runtime: need access level for our SDK onboarding guide (Node + Python). If you want, we can push a quick repo with example calls in your repo.
2) Auth: preference order we discussed — OIDC (client credentials) -> API key with mTLS as fallback. Please confirm if Okta metadata + client_id/client_secret is available.
3) Routing: we recommend latency-first routing for chat (route to dedicated low-latency pool) and cost-first for nightly batch embedding jobs. Do you want per-route tags in the API (e.g., route=chat, route=batch)?
4) Structured output/tool calling: we propose JSON-style tool defs (attached proto_tool_defs.json) that list function names, inputs, and success/fail codes. Examples: ticket_lookup({ticket_id}), product_search({query, filters}). We also recommend a small envelope: {tool, args, confidence, fallback_text}.
5) Embeddings & reranker: sample dataset (1000 tickets) so we can run embeddings locally and tune reranker thresholds. If possible, share a scrubbed CSV with id,text,label.
6) Failure modes: propose 3-tier fallback — cache result -> lightweight heuristic -> human handoff. Define timeout budget per tool call (default 150ms).

Attachments: Quantify_POC_scope_v1.pdf (scope); auth_diagram.png (depicts OIDC flow); proto_tool_defs.json (function stubs).

Next steps (proposed) — please confirm:
- You share Okta/Azure metadata + sample dataset by Wed (11/24)
- Schedule architecture deep-dive next week (30–45m) — suggested slots Tue/Wed 10–12 PT
- We send a slim SOW + milestone schedule after deep-dive (Marissa will lead commercial terms)

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + POC checklist (auth, routing, tool-calling)

Aisha — thanks for the crisp summary. Quick clarifications from our side:
1) Auth: we prefer OIDC via Azure AD (client credentials). Okta is not our central IdP anymore. I can share metadata + a service account with limited scope (client_id, client_secret) once our security team signs the NDA addendum.
2) VPC / networking: yes, private peering is required. We use a shared transit VPC; we'll need IP allowlist and a short list of egress domains for redwood endpoints.
3) Tool calls: product_search must hit our internal catalog service (hosted in our VPC) — it cannot egress to public endpoints. We'll need to run a lightweight connector in our VPC or allow Redwood Private deployment.
4) Failure handling: 150ms timeout for upstream services is okay as a starting point, but we may need a 2nd-tier 500ms fallback to return cached or best-effort results.

We'll aim to share:
- Azure AD metadata + contact for our infra SRE (Ishan)
- Scrubbed sample tickets (csv)
- Network allowlist requirements

One ask for clarification: for parallel tool invocation, does Redwood return a single merged structured envelope or multiple tool responses that the client reconciles? We prefer a single deterministic envelope if possible.

—Sunil
Sunil Park
CTO, Quantify Labs

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 09:12 Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sunil Park <s.park@quantifylabs.com>, Eva Martinez <eva@quantifylabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + POC checklist (auth, routing, tool-calling)

Thanks — quick technical notes and proposed approach from the infra side.

1) Parallel tool model: Redwood can invoke multiple tool endpoints in parallel and then synthesize a single structured envelope that contains tool responses plus a provenance list. That envelope looks like: {request_id, tools: [{name, status, response, latency_ms}], synthesized_output}. We'll attach a small example in the architecture call. This matches the single-envelope preference noted by Sunil.

2) Connector options for private VPC access:
- Option A: Redwood Private (deploy connector in your VPC) — fastest to meet security needs but requires licensing.
- Option B: Lightweight sidecar that proxies to your internal services (reverse-proxy + mTLS) — lower Ops barrier; we can supply a Helm chart.

3) Auth flows: primary = OIDC client-credentials. For connector-to-service we support mTLS and short-lived signed tokens from our connector. We'll need Okta/Azure AD metadata; if your SRE prefers, we can integrate with your KMS for signed JWTs.

4) Structured output / function definitions: Ben asks we lock the initial tool set to 4–6 functions and use a strict JSON schema (attached proto_tool_defs.json) for the POC. If the model emits non-conforming output, runtime will route to a sanitizer step and optionally call a fallback tool that provides a safe canned response.

5) Timeouts & retries: default per-tool — timeout 150ms, retry 0 for critical upstreams (to avoid duplicate side effects). For read-only calls (product_search) we can allow 1 retry. Circuit-breakers: tripped after 3 failures per minute.

I'll prep a short technical agenda for the deep-dive (20m architecture + 20m connector/auth + 10m Q&A). Can someone propose 2 slots?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
